extracted.intended_audience: State environmental agencies and owners/operators of electric generating units (EGUs)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and technical requirements for monitoring, calculating, recordkeeping, reporting, and State plan submittals to demonstrate compliance with EPA CO2 emissions standards for affected electric generating units (EGUs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculate P_gross/net (Equation 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate P_gross/net for an affected EGU (or group of EGUs sharing a monitored common stack) using Equation 1. All terms must be expressed in units of MWh. To convert each hourly gross or net energy output value reported under 40 CFR part 75 to MWh, multiply by the corresponding EGU or stack operating time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines P_GROSS/NET as gross or net energy output for each valid operating hour (MWh). Includes component terms: (PE)ST (steam turbine electric + mechanical output), (PE)CT (combustion turbine output), (PE)IE (integrated equipment electric/mechanical output), (PE)A (electric energy used for auxiliary loads), (PT)PS (useful thermal steam output used for non-electric applications), (PT)HR (non-steam useful thermal output from heat recovery), (PT)IE (useful thermal output from integrated equipment), and TDF (transmission and distribution factor). All hourly values must be in MWh; any hour without valid data counts as zero for calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculate P_t_PS for combined heat and power (Equation 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable (e.g., for combined heat and power), calculate (Pt)PS using Equation 2, which converts measured steam flow and enthalpy to MWh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equation uses Q_M (measured steam flow in kg or lbs), H (enthalpy of steam at measured temperature and pressure relative to SATP or energy in condensate return), and CF (conversion factor: 3.6 × 10^9 J/MWh or 3.413 × 10^6 BTU/MWh). Ensure units are consistent when computing useful thermal output in MWh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate-based CO2 emissions rate calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: For rate-based standards, sum P_gross/net over all valid operating hours and divide the total CO2 mass emissions for the valid operating hours by the sum of the P_gross/net values to determine the CO2 emissions rate (lb/gross or net MWh).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CO2 mass emissions values from monitoring (paragraph (a)(3)(v) or (a)(4)(v)). Ensure only 'valid operating hours' (per the rule) are included in both the numerator and denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common stack monitoring option (§60.13(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs share a common exhaust gas stack and are subject to the same emissions standard, the owner/operator may monitor hourly CO2 mass emissions at the common stack instead of monitoring each EGU separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using common-stack monitoring, hourly gross or net electric output for the common stack must equal the sum of the hourly gross or net electric outputs of the individual affected EGUs and operating time must be expressed as 'stack operating hours' (per 40 CFR 72.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple stacks or ducts monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: If exhaust gases are emitted through multiple stacks (or routed to a common stack through multiple ducts and monitoring is elected in the ducts), the hourly CO2 mass emissions and stack operating time at each stack or duct must be monitored separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine compliance by summing the CO2 mass emissions measured at individual stacks/ducts and dividing by the gross or net energy output for the affected EGU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment when EGUs serve a common generator
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs serve a common electric generator, apportion the combined hourly gross or net energy output to individual EGUs according to the fraction of the total steam load contributed by each EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, if the EGUs are identical, apportion combined hourly gross or net electrical load according to the fraction of the total heat input contributed by each EGU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly fuel usage reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must measure and report monthly fuel usage for each affected source subject to standards of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each monthly report must include: (i) the calendar month during which the fuel was used; (ii) each type of fuel used during that month; and (iii) quantity of each type of fuel combusted in the calendar month with units of measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping retention durations and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must require owners/operators to maintain records for at least 5 years following each occurrence, measurement, maintenance, corrective action, report, or record. Owners/operators must keep each record on site for at least 2 years after the date of each occurrence; remaining years may be kept off site and electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must be maintained according to §60.7 and be in a form suitable and readily available for expeditious review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records to be maintained for demonstrating compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must keep all documents, data files, calculations, and methods used to demonstrate compliance with an affected EGU's standard of performance; copies of reports submitted to the State; and data required to be recorded by 40 CFR part 75 subpart F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These records must be available for inspection and maintained in a retrievable format for the required retention period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner/operator reporting: include all hourly CO2 emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports submitted to the State must include all hourly CO2 emissions for each affected EGU (or group of EGUs sharing a monitored common stack).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required baseline reporting element for each affected EGU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate-based standards: required hourly and summary reporting elements
rubrics_metrics.description: For rate-based standards each report must include specific hourly values and summaries for valid operating hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items: (i) hourly CO2 mass emission rate values (tons/hr) and unit (or stack) operating times as monitored under part 75; (ii) hourly gross or net electric output and P_gross/net values for each valid hour; (iii) calculated CO2 mass emissions (lb) for each valid hour; (iv) sum of hourly gross or net energy outputs and sum of hourly CO2 mass emissions for all valid hours; (v) calculated CO2 mass emission rate (lbs/gross or net MWh).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report must include standard of performance and demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Each affected EGU report must include the applicable standard of performance and a demonstration that the EGU met the standard, including the affected EGU's calculated emission performance as a CO2 emission rate in units of the standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State must require owner/operator to include demonstration and calculated performance in annual or required reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow additional State plan monitoring/recordkeeping/reporting (§60.5740b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must follow any additional monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements included in the approved State plan under §60.5740b, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-specific requirements may impose more stringent or additional procedures beyond the federal subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements when CO2 is captured to meet standard
rubrics_metrics.description: If an affected EGU captures CO2 to meet the applicable standard of performance, the owner/operator must report in accordance with 40 CFR part 98 subpart PP and either: (1) part 98 subpart RR or VV if injection occurs on-site; (2) transfer captured CO2 to a facility reporting under part 98 subpart RR or VV if injection occurs off-site; or (3) transfer to a facility that has an EPA innovative technology waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting pathway depends on whether injection is on-site or off-site. Ensure reporting is consistent with part 98 subparts cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver process for requiring transfer of captured CO2
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may request an Administrator waiver of the requirement that captured CO2 be transferred to a facility reporting under part 98 subpart RR or VV. To receive a waiver, the applicant must demonstrate that its technology will store CO2 as effectively as geologic sequestration and will not cause/unreasonably contribute to risk to public health, welfare, or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator considers operating history, whether technology increases emissions of other pollutants, permanence of CO2 storage, may require tests, may grant conditional approval with monitoring/reporting conditions, may withdraw approval upon evidence of releases, and will provide public notice of petitions and proposed actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan submittal procedures via SPeCS/CDX and CBI handling
rubrics_metrics.description: All State plan submittals, supporting materials, revisions, and State reports must be submitted through EPA's State Plan Electronic Collection System (SPeCS) accessed via CDX. States claiming confidential business information (CBI) must submit that information on electronic storage media to the EPA CBI Office, clearly marked as CBI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic media must be mailed to the specified EPA address for CBI. Submittals claiming CBI should include clear markings and follow instructions for CBI handling; otherwise State plan material submitted via SPeCS will be processed through CDX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized official for State plan submittal
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a submittal by the Governor or the Governor's designee via electronic submission through SPeCS shall be considered an official submittal to the EPA under this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Governor designates another official, EPA must be notified via letter prior to the May 11, 2026 deadline so the designee can submit. Documentation of prior delegations may be submitted in lieu of a new letter. Required contact info includes title, organization, and email address for designee and preparers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submittal format: non-editable and editable copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be in a non-editable format. In addition, all State plan components designated as federally enforceable must also be submitted in an editable version. Following approval, States must provide editable copies of any revisions to federally enforceable components and indicate changes (e.g., redline/strikethrough).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editable copies must clearly show changes made at the State level. Changes are not part of the State plan until formally approved by EPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report to EPA: required contents (§60.5870b)
rubrics_metrics.description: States must submit an annual report to EPA (by March 1 following each calendar year) containing specified information about affected EGUs and State plan implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required elements include: (1) emissions performance achieved by each affected EGU and compliance status; (2) comparison of CO2 standard vs. actual performance for each EGU; (3) sum of CO2 emissions, gross energy output, and heat input by fuel type for each EGU; (4) enforcement actions initiated; (5) achievement of increments of progress required by State plan; (6) identification of designated facilities that ceased operation during the period; (7) emission inventory data for facilities that began operation during the period; (8) additional data needed to update prior submissions; (9) copies of technical performance testing reports with concurrent process data; (10) all other required information per State plan (§60.5740b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping/reporting for EGUs committed to permanent cessation by Jan 1, 2032
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of EGUs that committed to permanently cease operations by Jan 1, 2032 must maintain records and submit reports as specified: an initial report five years before planned cessation (or by State plan submission date), annual status reports for remaining years, and a final report within 6 months following committed closure documenting actions to ensure cessation is permanent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial report must include: (i) summary of process steps and timing required to permanently cease operations (e.g., notices to reliability authorities, retirement filings); and (ii) supporting regulatory documents (correspondence and official filings with RTO/ISO/BA/PUC, deactivation-related reliability assessments, SEC filings, integrated resource plans, reliability analyses, notifications altering timing, etc.). Annual reports must document progress on process steps and supporting regulatory documents. Final report must document post-cessation actions (e.g., decommissioning filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: CEDRI submission, public availability, and CBI handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Notifications or reports that must be submitted under the specified procedures must be submitted to EPA via CEDRI through CDX. The EPA will make all information submitted through CEDRI available to the public without further notice; do not use CEDRI to submit information claimed as CBI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claiming CBI for part of a submission, also submit the complete file including CBI to the EPA CBI Office by the prescribed CBI procedures and omit CBI when submitting via CDX/CEDRI. Emissions data are not entitled to confidential treatment under CAA section 114(c) and will be made public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred and alternative methods to transmit CBI
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred method to provide CBI is electronic transmission (email attachments, FTP, or online file sharing) to OAQPS CBI Office at oaqpscbi@epa.gov. If electronic transmission is not possible, mail double-wrapped physical media to the specified EPA address and mark clearly as CBI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assistance is needed for large files, contact oaqpscbi@epa.gov to request a file transfer link. Ensure CBI markings do not show through the outer envelope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic records and on-site availability for CEDRI submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Records submitted electronically via CEDRI may be maintained in electronic format; this does not affect the requirement to make records, data, and reports available upon request to a delegated air agency or the EPA during on-site compliance evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain electronic copies in retrievable form and ensure timely provision during inspections or compliance evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming EPA system outage for electronic submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If precluded from accessing CEDRI/CDX due to an EPA system outage within five business days prior to the submission deadline, an owner/operator may assert a claim of EPA system outage for failure to timely comply, subject to specified requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must notify Administrator in writing as soon as possible after knowing about the delay; provide dates/times of attempted access and unavailability, rationale attributing delay to EPA outage, description of measures to minimize delay, and proposed date to report (or actual report date). Acceptance of the claim and any extension is at Administrator's discretion. Report must be submitted electronically as soon as possible after outage resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Force majeure claims for electronic submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators may assert a force majeure claim for failure to timely submit electronically if a qualifying event (e.g., acts of nature, war/terrorism, large-scale power outage, equipment failure) prevents timely submission within five business days prior to the due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must notify Administrator in writing as soon as possible and provide a written description of the force majeure event, rationale attributing delay to the event, measures taken to minimize delay, and the proposed date to report (or actual report date). Acceptance is at Administrator's sole discretion. Reporting must occur as soon as possible after the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives to electronic reporting require Administrator approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Any alternatives to required electronic reporting under this subpart must be approved by the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a facility proposes an alternative submission method, obtain prior approval from the Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Affected electric generating unit (Affected EGU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected EGU means a steam generating unit that meets the relevant applicability conditions in §60.5845b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to determine which units fall under the rule's monitoring/reporting/standards requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Annual capacity factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual capacity factor means the ratio between the actual heat input to an EGU during a calendar year and the potential heat input if the EGU were operated for 8,760 hours at base load rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for performance/operational calculations and classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Base load rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Base load rating means the maximum heat input an EGU can combust on a steady-state basis as determined by the EGU's physical design and characteristics at ISO conditions. For stationary combustion turbines or IGCC, base load rating includes heat input from duct burners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in capacity factor and related calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Coal-fired steam generating unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Coal-fired steam generating unit means an electric utility steam generating unit or IGCC unit that burns coal for more than 10.0% of average annual heat input during any continuous 3-calendar-year period after Dec 31, 2029, or more than 15.0% of annual heat input during any one calendar year after Dec 31, 2029, or that retains capability to fire coal after Dec 31, 2029.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold percentages determine coal-fired status for regulatory classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Combined cycle unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Combined cycle unit means a stationary combustion turbine from which turbine exhaust heat is recovered by a heat recovery steam generating unit (HRSG) to generate additional electricity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to classify unit types and applicable monitoring/calculation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Combined heat and power unit (CHP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combined heat and power unit (cogeneration) means an electric generating unit that uses a steam-generating unit or stationary combustion turbine to simultaneously produce both electric (or mechanical) and useful thermal output from the same primary energy source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers special calculation rules (e.g., P_gross/net components, TDF) when at least 20% of output is useful thermal on a 12-month rolling basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Compliance period
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance period means an annual (calendar year) period for an affected EGU to comply with a standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to define reporting periods and annual summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Derate
rubrics_metrics.description: Derate means a decrease in the available capacity of an EGU due to system/equipment modification or discounting a portion of capacity for planning purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derate affects calculations of available capacity and may influence base load rating and capacity factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Fossil fuel
rubrics_metrics.description: Fossil fuel means natural gas, petroleum, coal, and any form of solid, liquid, or gaseous fuel derived from such material for creating useful heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine applicability and unit classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Gross energy output
rubrics_metrics.description: Gross energy output means: (1) for stationary combustion turbines and IGCC, the gross electric or direct mechanical output from the EGU plus 100% of the useful thermal output; (2) for steam generating units, gross electric/mechanical output minus electricity used to power feedwater pumps plus 100% of useful thermal output; (3) for CHP facilities meeting the 20% thermal output threshold, a specified formula dividing net electric/mechanical outputs by 0.95 plus 100% of useful thermal output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different unit types have differing methods for computing gross energy output; apply the correct clause for the unit's configuration and the CHP threshold where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Heat recovery steam generating unit (HRSG)
rubrics_metrics.description: HRSG means a unit where hot exhaust gases from the combustion turbine are routed to extract heat and generate useful output; HRSGs can be used with or without duct burners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant for combined cycle and IGCC classifications and energy output accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Integrated gasification combined cycle facility (IGCC)
rubrics_metrics.description: IGCC means a combined cycle facility designed to burn fuels containing 50% or more solid-derived fuel (by heat input) plus any integrated equipment that provides electricity or useful thermal output to the affected facility or auxiliary equipment; Administrator may waive the 50% during certain startup/shutdown periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IGCC classification affects calculation of gross/net energy output and applicability of certain requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: ISO conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: ISO conditions means 288 Kelvin (15 °C), 60% relative humidity, and 101.3 kilopascals pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as reference conditions for base load rating and other standard calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Mechanical output
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanical output means useful mechanical energy not used to operate the facility, generate electricity/thermal output, or enhance facility performance; horsepower-hour must be converted to MWh by multiplying by 745.7 then dividing by 1,000,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mechanical output in gross/net energy output calculations where applicable, after unit conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Nameplate capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Nameplate capacity means, starting from initial installation, the maximum electrical generating output a generator/prime mover is capable of producing (MWe, rounded to nearest tenth) on a steady-state basis during continuous operation as specified by the manufacturer, or as updated after a physical change resulting in increased capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for unit classification, planning, and some reporting elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Natural gas
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural gas means a fluid mixture of hydrocarbons (e.g., methane, ethane, propane) composed of at least 70% methane by volume or gross calorific value between 35 and 41 MJ per dry standard cubic meter, that remains gaseous under ISO conditions; excludes landfill gas, digester gas, refinery gas, sour gas, blast furnace gas, coal-derived gas, producer gas, coke oven gas, or any gaseous fuel with highly variable CO2 content or heating value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to classify fuel types for fuel usage reporting and unit definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Natural gas-fired steam generating unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural gas-fired steam generating unit means an electric utility steam generating unit that is not coal-fired or oil-fired, no longer retains capability to fire coal after Dec 31, 2029, and burns natural gas for >10% of average annual heat input over a continuous 3-calendar-year period after Dec 31, 2029, or >15% in any one calendar year after Dec 31, 2029.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to classify steam units by fuel type for regulatory applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Net electric output
rubrics_metrics.description: Net electric output means the gross generation measured at generator terminals less electricity used to operate the plant (auxiliary loads) including fuel handling, pumps, fans, pollution control equipment, other electricity needs, and transformer losses as measured at the transmission side of the step up transformer (point of sale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use net electric output when reporting net energy output values and for compliance rate denominators where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Net energy output
rubrics_metrics.description: Net energy output means: (1) net electric or mechanical output from the facility plus 100% of useful thermal output measured relative to SATP that is not used to generate additional electric/mechanical output or to enhance unit performance; (2) for CHP facilities meeting the 20% thresholds, the net electric/mechanical output divided by 0.95 plus 100% of useful thermal output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the correct clause depending on CHP thresholds to compute net energy output for rate-based calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Oil-fired steam generating unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Oil-fired steam generating unit means an electric utility steam generating unit that is not coal-fired, no longer retains capability to fire coal after Dec 31, 2029, and burns oil for >10% of average annual heat input over any continuous 3-calendar-year period after Dec 31, 2029, or >15% in any calendar year after Dec 31, 2029.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for fuel-based classification and applicability determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Standard ambient temperature and pressure (SATP)
rubrics_metrics.description: SATP conditions means 298.15 Kelvin (25 °C) and 100.0 kilopascals pressure. The enthalpy of water at SATP conditions is 50 Btu/lb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the reference for measuring useful thermal outputs when converting to MWh in thermal calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: State agent
rubrics_metrics.description: State agent means an entity acting on behalf of the State, with the legal authority of the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be relevant for State plan submissions or delegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Stationary combustion turbine
rubrics_metrics.description: Stationary combustion turbine means all equipment including turbine engine, fuel/air/lubrication/exhaust systems, controls (except emissions control equipment), heat recovery system, fuel compressor/heater/pump, post-combustion emission control technology, and any ancillary components comprising simple cycle, combined cycle, CHP turbine-based systems plus any integrated equipment that provides electricity or useful thermal output to the turbine, heat recovery system, or auxiliary equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad equipment definition used to determine applicability of monitoring and calculation rules.
